en.html:
...I was sitting among the trees. Hikaru was in my arms, breathing quietly in her sleep.

Sitting, I say. Perhaps even that was giving myself too much credit. Perhaps I had simply stopped being able to move.

My leg muscles had tightened completely. Standing up itself looked beyond me. How far had I run? Wounds all over, and plenty of blood lost.

My consciousness had gone somewhere else. From the moment I carried Hikaru out of the Horigoe residence until now, staring blankly about me—nothing. Not one scrap of memory.

Surely I had not been running for more than a whole day. It should still be the same night. A few hours, perhaps... Nahin, perhaps less even than that.

Almost pure guesswork, but the land around me felt like Izu. Not so different from Horigoe.

そうにない。

　光を抱えて堀越御所を飛び出してから――いま呆然
と周囲を見回しているこの瞬間まで。記憶は全き空白
で、何も残っていなかった。

から、まだ同じ夜の内であろう。
　おそらく、あれから数時間程……いや、実はもっと
短いのかもしれない。

　ほとんど勘でしかないが、辺りの風土も伊豆のもの、
堀越のそれとそう違いはないと思える。

en.html:
—Ab kya? What should I do now?

A thoroughly foolish question, whichever way one looked at it. No need to ask it now. Not the time to ask it now. No use asking it now either.

The answer was clear.
What I had to do, I knew very well.

So I stopped thinking.
That answer I did not need. Did not want.

I did not want to know.
Even if I knew already... let me pretend while I still could. Itna toh karne do.

I settled Hikaru in my arms again and lowered my face. Her quiet sleeping breath touched my cheek.

A little sleep first.
Whatever had to be thought about, I could think about after waking.

For now, sleep. Let me stay in this last illusion.
Like this... always. Always, keeping Hikaru safe...

いう……。

Hikaru said it smiling, both arms spread, as though tasting the mountain's night breeze.

Hikaru.

...Silver Star.

They said Silver Star was the dream of Hikaru Minato. Standing in that moonlight, yes, she did look like something from a dream.

But hollow? Weak? Nothing of the sort.
There was power. Power spilling over!

This was supposed to be a dream?
With so much strength in it?

Perhaps I was the one who had dreamed some nonsense. Somewhere in these mountains I had wandered into, foxes or tanuki had played their tricks on me...

That explanation, at least—right now, I could swallow.

Once I said it aloud, the matter was settled.

Top-class bakwaas.
Something that plainly did not look like a dream: are you a dream? Something I believed was a dream: are you a dream?

Either way, the man asking had his brain wiring cut somewhere. It was me only. Something was wrong with me...

Hikaru would make nothing of it. She would draw her brows together, look puzzled, ask what I meant—
